newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says shipwreck makes Albanian mission urgent.
newsitem.headline: Italy says shipwreck makes Albanian mission urgent.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that the sinking of a refugee boat had made an international mission to help Albania more urgent as a row raged over the number of people who may have died.
Prodi also told reporters that a navy operation to patrol the southern Adriatic and stem a tide of refugees would continue because it had Albanian government approval.
"This event shows that the international operation to help Albania has to begin as soon as possible," Prodi said.
The U.N. Security Council late on Friday authorised the mission to help the country recover from violence and anarchy.
Franz Vranitzky, the envoy of Europe's top security body the OSCE, said an Italian-led force to guard aid deliveries could be dispatched within two weeks.

Survivors of the sinking accident said more than 100 refugees may have been on the ageing Russian-made harbour patrol craft when it went down on Friday night after colliding with a navy vessel patrolling the Adriatic.
Italy's top navy official said that while he could not exclude that more than four people had died, he believed the boat was too small to have contained many people below deck.
Admiral Angelo Mariani told a news conference that 34 people were rescued after the accident in international waters between Italy and Albania and four bodies had been recovered.
"I cannot exclude unfortunately that there were other people on board but I don't think there could have been too many more below deck," Mariani said.
Coastguards said the search for survivors or bodies was being hampered by bad weather at sea.

Survivors among the rescued passengers arriving in the southern port of Brindisi during the night feared many more than four had perished. Most placed the number of passengers at between 70 and more than 100, a number of them children.
"More than 50 of us died," one Albanian man shouted to reporters gathered on the dock.
The Italian news agency Ansa, in a report from Vlore, the Albanian port from where the boat left, quoted witnesses as saying that there were "no fewer than 120 people" on board.
"I can't believe that there were that many people on board ... it seems exaggerated to me that there could have been 100...," Mariani said in response to questions.
Mariani said he believed that such a figure was unlikely since the boat was about 20 metres long, usually carried a crew of eight, and had limited passenger space below deck.

The navy said there were some 30 people on the deck when the boat capsized. Officers on the corvette Sibilla, which was in collision with the Albanian boat, had seen no sign of passengers below deck through the boat's portholes.
The navy said the Sibilla hit the Albanian boat after it had cut across its bows abruptly. It sank about an hour later.
"As far as we are concerned, it was they who hit us," the admiral said. "The accident happened because the Albanian ship behaved in an unpredictable and irresponsible way."
Mariani said Tirana had informed Italy that the Albanian boat was piloted by "local criminals".
Italy, concerned that many Albanian refugees are looking for a better life abroad rather than fleeing real danger, has ordered the navy to patrol the Adriatic to halt the flow.
The operation involves intercepting Albanian ships outside Italian waters and advising them to turn back.
Some politicians criticised the navy actions while others pointed the finger at Albania. Fringe groups called for the resignation of Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta.
More than 13,000 Albanians have reached Italy in the past two weeks on a flotilla of ancient boats after rebels in the south took control of towns in an armed insurrection.
The sinking was the first incident involving fatalities since the exodus began on March 13.
